1.why: All nine screens use a calm single-card layout with no animations, moving images, or pop-ups, though the ever-present technical Logs panel adds unnecessary visual clutter below the main task.

2.why: Large headings, bold dark-blue primary buttons, and a blue focus ring on the active field make the key elements clearly stand out on every screen.

3.why: Each page presents essentially one task with a single prominent button, but the user must hunt through the Logs panel to find the required MFA codes, which slows down locating what she needs.

4.why: The flow spans nine steps (request, token, MFA code, password creation with 14–128 character upper/lower/number/symbol rules, sign-in, second MFA code, acceptance), imposing many rules and steps to remember.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, passkey option, show/hide password toggle, or explicit password-manager/autofill support appears on any screen; only plain masked input fields are shown.

6.why: No saved or familiar items are surfaced — the sign-in page does not display the account identity, no remembered device or prefilled contact is shown, and every step demands fresh entry.

7.why: Text throughout is short and plain (e.g., 'Sign in to acknowledge the updated privacy statement'), with only minor jargon such as 'MFA code' and 'token' in the repeated security notice.

8.why: No error message is shown on any of the nine screens, so the claim that error messages describe the problem and its fix cannot be confirmed or denied from what was observed.

9.why: Step 1 gives a concrete example ('name@example.org or +15551234567'), and helper hints appear elsewhere ('the test code is in the Logs panel'), though the password step states rules without an example.

10.why: Only password plus six-digit code authentication exists — there is no face login or alternative choice — though the few options that are offered (simulated link vs. manual token entry) are labeled clearly.

11.why: Every screen offers at most one primary button plus a single secondary link, so the user is never confronted with more than one or two choices at a time.

12.why: Actions produce clear confirmations — the blue 'recovery instructions have been prepared' banner and the final 'Privacy statement accepted... securely recorded' page — though intermediate steps confirm only by advancing to the next page.

13.why: Each new step carries a short tip ('Tokens are short-lived and can only be used once', the password rule hint, the repeated safe-authentication notice), but no help link or support contact is provided.

14.why: No resend, retry, or recovery-from-mistake mechanism is visible on any screen, and the warning that tokens are 'short-lived and can only be used once' implies a mistake may force restarting the whole flow.

15.why: All nine screens share the identical header, centered white card, typography, button styling, and repeated green security notice, making the design highly consistent and learnable.
